text: A structural mismatch is asserted before any pixel comparison, and fails without reporting a pixel number at all. GRADED ON A SPLIT, snorkeltoast's own framing after they corrected themselves upward: the DETECTOR is red-proved on the real artifact in the run behind FLOORS.md -- cmd_redproof assertion 2 removes a slide from the payload and requires compare_structure to fail, observed at snorkeltoast 28b4127 as "79 structural difference(s), first: slide COUNT differs: reference 22, new 21". CITE THAT RUN AND NOT THE EARLIER redproof2.log, which reports the identical figure from a strictly weaker setup: it ran against a control carrying no min_defect, so slides 13 and 14 were excluded as UNDECIDED and only 18 slides were graded, where the 28b4127 run uses ctl10 -- the control FLOORS.md is generated from -- and grades 20 with one exclusion. THE CALLER'S ORDERING IS INSPECTION ONLY and redproof is candid about it in its own output, which asserts the ordering by pointing at cmd_compare's STRUCTURE block rather than observing cmd_compare refuse. So the mechanism that finds a mismatch has been made to fire against a real injury; the mechanism that guarantees no pixel number is printed first has been read, not run. THE ROW'S WORD "ids" IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN FAILED: slides carry no id -- collect_segment does not put a segment's `id:` into the payload -- and identity is position plus every rendering parameter except pixels, which is strictly STRONGER than an id would give. The absence is not a gap and must not be read as one. Discharged when cmd_compare's die-before-any-pixel-number is observed rather than inspected.

An observation at a later die point dominates every earlier one on a linear path. THE ROW'S WORD "ids" IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN FAILED: slides carry no id -- collect_segment does not put a segment's id: into the payload -- and identity is position plus every rendering parameter except pixels, which is strictly STRONGER than an id would give. The absence is not a gap.
